mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a term premium compression, reducing expected equity discount rates and pushing 20-day S&P 500 forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or flat despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for ≥2 consecutive months prior.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < previous month and INDPRO > previous month) signals weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND INDPRO > previous month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and persistent across 5 such labor signal events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 10% year-over-year coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), indicating strong consumer demand without supply constraints, which drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY > +10% AND INDPRO < previous month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically significant vs. baseline in 10 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months predicts a supply-side recession, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers sharply within 2 months, and 20-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure that raises policy rate expectations, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive in 4 out of 10 such CPI surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite UNRATE remaining below 4% for ≥3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 12-month averages for three months indicates robust overall demand, which predicts positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12M avg AND INDPRO > 12M avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative in 4 out of 6 such demand expansion periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence catalog) cannot be used; instead, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 (monthly index) while payrolls (PAYEMS) remain stable suggests supply-side softness, predicting negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers sharply within 2 months and 20-day returns are positive.
